title: A Recipe for the Prom
premise: Theo Ravensworth has spent three years holding her family together in the dying mill town of Halloway Falls, where the annual Founders' Prom is the last thread binding the community. When her college essay forces her to admit she's drowning, and she discovers the town council plans to sell the grange hall—the Prom's historic home—to a developer, Theo can no longer stay invisible. Rallying her scattered siblings, her best friend Dev, and a town that's forgotten how to hope, she fights to save the Prom while learning that loyalty sometimes means telling the truth she's been hiding: she's exhausted, she's angry, and she wants a life of her own. In the end, the Prom happens in a half-restored hall lit by paper lanterns, Theo submits the essay that got her in, and she leaves for college knowing her family—and her town—finally know how to stand without her holding them up.
about_author: I. M. Zhou grew up in a small rust-belt town where the community center's annual dance was the social event of the year, and she never stopped believing that ordinary places hold extraordinary stories. She writes young adult fiction about siblings, small towns, and the quiet heroism of teenagers nobody notices until it's too late to ignore them.

chapters.title: Fine, Obviously
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A chaotic morning—burnt pancakes, a lost permission slip, mom's night-shift note—establishes the Ravensworth household Theo runs. She insists to everyone, including herself, that everything is fine. Emotional beat: weary competence masking exhaustion.

chapters.title: The Question on Page Three
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. In English class, the college essay prompt asks: 'Describe a moment that changed you.' Theo writes a safe, forgettable draft about volunteering. Her teacher, Ms. Okafor, writes one word in red: 'Honesty?' Emotional beat: first crack in the armor.

chapters.title: Grange Hall Ghosts
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Sent to retrieve a folding table from the old grange hall, Theo wanders the dusty home of the Founders' Prom, finding her parents' names on the 1998 sweetheart board. A notice taped to the door: PUBLIC HEARING — SALE OF PROPERTY. Emotional beat: grief for something not yet gone.

chapters.title: Dev Sees Everything
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev, Theo's best friend and secret crush, watches her juggle everything and calls her out gently over milkshakes. He's noticed the developer's survey stakes near the hall. Emotional beat: being truly seen is terrifying and wonderful.

chapters.title: Little Generals
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Siblings Junie, Marcus, and Priya each reveal they've noticed Theo's strain in different ways—Junie's been skipping choir to babysit. The family has its first honest fight in years. Emotional beat: love expressed as resentment, then tenderness.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The council hearing is stacked: the developer promises jobs, the town is desperate, and the hall's defenders are few and scattered. Theo speaks up unprepared, her voice shaking, and something shifts in the room. Emotional beat: the invisible girl becomes visible.

chapters.title: Ninety Days
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The council grants a compromise: if the Prom happens as it has for eighty years, the sale stalls; fail, and the hall goes. Theo forms a committee of misfits. Dev volunteers, hiding that his own family is moving away in June. Emotional beat: hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: Mom Comes Home Early
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Mom, home before dawn, finds Theo's college essay draft on the kitchen table and reads the raw second attempt. Instead of anger: her own confession of how the Prom saved her, young and alone, decades ago. Emotional beat: inheritance of survival.

chapters.title: Fundraisers and Fiascos
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The siblings' bake sale/car wash/spaghetti dinner montage goes hilariously wrong but raises real money—and real attention. Priya, the observer, narrates her siblings with sharp love. Emotional beat: family as a machine that works when it argues.

chapters.title: The Developer's Daughter
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Chloe Marsh, daughter of the developer, transfers into Theo's class—and asks to join the Prom committee, to her father's fury. Theo doesn't trust her. Emotional beat: suspicion as a mirror for Theo's own guardedness.

chapters.title: What Dev Isn't Saying
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev's family's moving truck gets a date: June 1st, the week after the Prom. He almost tells Theo at lantern-hanging practice and can't. Instead, he kisses her under the half-strung lights. Emotional beat: sweetness shadowed by the unsaid.

chapters.title: Vandalism
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The grange hall is vandalized overnight—windows smashed, the sweetheart board destroyed. The town blames the developer; Theo suspects something closer to home. Emotional beat: the cost of caring, and the temptation to quit.

chapters.title: Marcus's Secret
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus confesses: he and friends broke a window weeks ago goofing off; tonight's damage was someone else. His guilt unravels into the real discovery—Councilman Reed has been sabotaging the hall to force the sale. Emotional beat: a boy learning that truth costs less than lies.

chapters.title: Proof and Price
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo and Chloe team up to dig into Reed's dealings with the developer—Chloe risking her father's business. They find the paper trail. Emotional beat: enemies becoming allies over shared integrity.

chapters.title: The Essay
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo finally writes the honest essay: about raising her siblings, about the Prom, about wanting to leave and being terrified that everything she loves falls apart without her. She submits it and sobs in the school parking lot. Emotional beat: release.

chapters.title: Reed Strikes Back
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Reed accuses Theo's committee of the vandalism and of misusing funds; the town turns, sponsors pull out, and Mom is threatened at work. Dev watches Theo nearly break—and finally admits his family is leaving. Emotional beat: the bottom falling out.

chapters.title: Everything Falls Apart
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. With the fund frozen and the family fighting, Theo does what she always does: tries to fix it all alone, and collapses—literally, from exhaustion, in the hall. Mom finds her. The truth comes out: Theo has been drowning for three years. Emotional beat: surrender.

chapters.title: The Town Remembers
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. While Theo recovers, Junie quietly shows the town the sweetheart board's surviving fragments—eighty years of names, including half the council's own parents. Neighbors start showing up with hammers, casseroles, and cash. Emotional beat: belonging, earned.

chapters.title: Reckoning at the Council
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Armed with Chloe's documents, Marcus's testimony, and a packed room, Theo confronts Reed publicly. The council voids the emergency sale measure; the developer, shamed by his own daughter, withdraws. Emotional beat: justice without cruelty—Theo chooses mercy.

chapters.title: Prom Eve
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The hall glows, restored by a hundred hands. Dev helps Theo pin up her hair, both knowing June 1st is coming. They agree: love honestly held is better than love quietly hidden. Emotional beat: bittersweet courage.

chapters.title: The Founders' Prom
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The Prom happens—imperfect, crowded, luminous. Mom dances with all four kids; the sweetheart board is rehung with a new photo of the Ravensworths. Dev and Theo dance under the lanterns they strung together. Emotional beat: joy that doesn't deny the cost.

chapters.title: What I'm Taking With Me
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, epilogue. Acceptance letter in hand, Theo packs not to escape but to begin. The family runs the morning without her—messily, fine, obviously. She drives past the grange hall, lit and alive, and waves. Emotional beat: belonging that travels.
